title: Individual Indian Money (IIM) / Whereabouts Unknown Account Investigation
summary: BTFA maintains IIM accounts for individual beneficiaries with trust money or assets and operates a public Whereabouts Unknown search for unclaimed accounts.
required_evidence: Identity documentation if BTFA identifies a possible account
next_actions: Search the official BTFA Whereabouts Unknown tool by last name and tribe.
If a possible match appears, contact BTFA to verify identity and account ownership.
Do not treat a same-name result as ownership until BTFA verifies it.

title: BIA Trust-Asset Probate / Inherited Trust Funds or Land
summary: When a deceased American Indian or Alaska Native owned trust/restricted land or trust funds, BIA compiles a probate package, OHA adjudicates heirship, land records are updated, and BTFA distributes trust funds.

predicate.label: Deceased Native ancestor may have owned trust/restricted assets
evidence: Death certificate or qualifying death evidence

required_evidence: Death certificate or other accepted proof of death
next_actions: Report the death or possible unprobated trust estate to BIA probate staff.
Ask BIA to verify whether the decedent owned trust/restricted assets at death.
If assets are confirmed, assemble the probate package and track the OHA decision.

sources.label: BIA Begin the Trust Asset Probate Process
BIA Division of Trust Asset Ownership and Title

title: Cherokee Dawes Allotment → Title/Probate Reconstruction
summary: NARA's Dawes land-allotment jackets can contain enrollment numbers, family relationships, physical locations, legal land descriptions, maps, correspondence, and contested-selection notices. These records can establish the starting parcel for a title/probate investigation but do not prove present ownership.

predicate.label: Known ancestor on a Cherokee Dawes final roll
evidence: Dawes enrollment number or census card if known

required_evidence: Allotment jacket and legal land description
next_actions: Locate the ancestor's Dawes enrollment record and allotment jacket.
Extract the exact township/range/section or other legal description.
Trace subsequent probate and title records; do not infer current ownership from the Dawes record alone.

title: Cherokee Nation Small Business Assistance Center
summary: Cherokee Nation SBAC supports Indian-owned businesses with access to capital for startup/expansion and business coaching. Published public pages do not contain every underwriting or program-specific rule, so program review remains required.
required_evidence: Financial information required by the selected SBAC program
next_actions: Contact Cherokee Nation SBAC and identify the current capital product that fits the use of funds.
Request the current application and underwriting checklist before transmitting sensitive documents.

title: Cherokee Nation TERO Indian-Owned Business Certification
summary: TERO certification can place a qualifying Indian-owned business on the Native-owned vendor list used in Cherokee Nation contracting and can provide preferential treatment in the bid process.

predicate.label: Indian owner is a member of a federally recognized tribe
At least 51% Indian ownership
evidence: Operating agreement, stock ledger, partnership or ownership documents

predicate.label: Indian ownership includes active operation and control

required_evidence: Documents requested for TERO site visit/review
next_actions: Download the current TERO certification application.
Assemble ownership and control evidence.
Submit to TERO; certification is decided by the TERO committee after review/site visit.

title: Cherokee Nation At-Large Undergraduate Scholarship
summary: Published for registered Cherokee citizens living outside the reservation who are working toward their first associate's or bachelor's degree and who apply for federal Pell aid through FAFSA.
next_actions: Open the current Cherokee Nation Higher Education application window and verify deadline/award terms.
Submit the at-large scholarship application with required documentation.

title: Cherokee Nation / BIA General Assistance
summary: BIA-funded General Assistance administered by Cherokee Nation for eligible Indian families addressing essential living needs; it is secondary to certain other benefit programs and requires documentation.

predicate.label: Member of a federally recognized tribe
Lives within Cherokee Nation jurisdiction for past six months
Insufficient resources for essential living needs

required_evidence: Other documents required for the household's circumstances
next_actions: Contact Cherokee Nation Human Services Family Assistance.
Verify whether TANF/SSI or other primary resources must be pursued first for the household.
Submit documentation for formal eligibility determination.

title: HUD Section 184 Indian Home Loan Guarantee
summary: Section 184 supports eligible Native borrowers financing a primary home through participating lenders. Tribal enrollment is only one part of eligibility; property area and lender underwriting must also be established.

predicate.label: Currently enrolled member of a federally recognized tribe

next_actions: Check whether the property county is currently eligible for Section 184.
Confirm the tribe participates for the proposed area when required.
Apply through a HUD-approved Section 184 lender for underwriting.

title: Cherokee Nation Career Readiness Act Vocational Training
summary: Cherokee Nation Career Services provides financial assistance for approved short-term vocational training leading to an industry-recognized credential, certification, or professional license; final approval depends on the training and workforce criteria.
next_actions: Confirm the proposed training is eligible and ordinarily completable within the program's allowed timeframe.
Apply through Cherokee Nation Career Services with the current program documentation.

title: 1975 Cherokee Indian Claims Commission Judgment-Fund Distribution
summary: Historical distribution only. The plan became effective November 5, 1975 and applications for the per-capita share had to be filed within one year. It is not a currently open descendant reparations program.
next_actions: Do not file a new claim under this closed 1975 application window.
If researching a deceased beneficiary's already-established property or trust proceeds, investigate the estate/IIM/probate path separately.

sources.label: BIA Cherokee Judgment Fund Plan Published
